 The disastrous joke that cost Matthew Rhys James Bond role revealed 
 By 
 Eric Todisco 
 Published 
 Nov. 20, 2026, 9:32 a.m. ET 
 See more of our coverage in your search results. 
 Make Page Six a Preferred Source 
 Matthew Rhys jokingly suggested that James Bond should have a “limp” when he was auditioning for Daniel Craig’s 007 role.
 Rhys, 52, said in a resurfaced 2023 interview with Conan O’Brien that during a meeting with the Bond producers, he was asked what he’d “do different” if he got the chance to play the iconic spy agent in 2006’s “Casino Royale.”
 “Is this a trick question, or is it a genuine question?” Rhys remembered thinking to himself at the time.

 The Welsh actor said he then “made the terrible” joke about Bond’s limp — which didn’t land well with the producers.
 “It got worse. It went very quiet,” he recalled. “So I thought I would double down, and said, ‘Eye patch.’ And then I just fell apart. And it lasted about 30 seconds after that.”
 Rhys added with a laugh, “That was my Bond moment. I think about that often.”
 8 
 Rhys (seen here) also jokingly suggested 007 should have an eyepatch. Getty Images for Netflix 
 8 
 Rhys said he lost out on the role to Daniel Craig, who played Bond for five films. Â©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection 
 The “Widow’s Bay” actor also admitted he “still doesn’t have a coherent answer that would’ve wowed” the Bond producers that day, and “often wonders” how Craig, 58, responded.
 Craig played Bond for five films, starting with “Casino Royale” and ending with 2021’s “No Time to Die.”
 O’Brien, 63, told Rhys he would’ve been “terrific” in the role of 007, to which Rhys replied, “Thank you. I told so many people I would be. I practically told my family I was going to be.”
 Rhys also recalled being among “a relatively large group of young white men who were invited to read ‘Casino Royale’, put on a nice, dark suit and go to the Broccolis’ office.”

 Over the years, Henry Cavill, Michael Fassbender, Sam Heughan, Alex O’Loughlin, James Purefoy, Antony Starr and Julian McMahon have all confirmed they were in the running to play Craig’s Bond.
 On Monday, Robert Pattinson was named the next actor to take on the coveted Bond role.
 “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement,” the “Twilight” star gushed in a statement. “I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

 8

 Nicholas Hoult, Josh O’Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden reportedly participated in screen tests for the upcoming 007 film.
 Denis Villeneuve, who worked with Pattinson in the upcoming “Dune: Part 3,” is directing the next Bond movie. 
 Amazon MGM Studios is producing the flick after the Broccoli family handed the franchise’s rights to the Jeff Bezos-owned company last year.
